quotes.quote: existing agent benchmarks are limited by trajectory-opaque grading, underspecified safety and robustness evaluation, and narrow coverage of modalities and interaction paradigms
We introduce Claw-Eval, an end-to-end evaluation suite addressing these gaps
three independent evidence channels: execution traces, audit logs, and environment snapshots
Multimodal tasks evaluate active perception and generation over rich media, including videos, documents, images, and code-generated visual artifacts.
the benchmark comprises 300 tasks spanning 9 fine-grained categories, organized into three complementary groups

Rubric items are either deterministic checks for objective conditions, such as file contents, tool parameters, or forbidden actions, or judgment-based checks using an LLM judge for open-ended criteria
Across the benchmark, the 300 tasks comprise 2,159 rubric items, averaging 7.2 items per task.
Multimodal (101 tasks) is restricted to the 9 vision-capable models

All models are accessed with default parameters except temperature=0 and thinking enabled where supported; each task runs in an isolated Docker sandbox for 3 independent trials with error injection rate 0.
Gemini-3-Flash (temperature=0) serves as the LLM judge for General and Multimodal rubric items requiring open-ended assessment
We report Score (average task score), Pass@3 (any trial exceeds 0.75), and Pass^3 (all three pass).
Multimodal tasks are substantially harder: the highest Pass^3 is only 25.7% (GPT-5.4)
Rankings shift across modalities: Claude-Opus-4.6 leads General but ranks second in Multimodal, while GPT-5.4 ranks third in General but first in Multimodal.
To understand how agents behave when tool calls intermittently fail, we evaluate three models on General tasks at error-injection rates of 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6
From rate 0.0 to 0.6, Pass@3 is nearly flat while Pass^3 drops sharply across different models, indicating that models can usually find one successful path but rarely all three.
Pass@3 remaining stable under error injection while Pass^3 dropping by up to 24 percentage points
Across five models and 2,000+ traces, the vanilla judge systematically underdetects issues caught by the hybrid pipeline
it misses 12/27 (44%) safety violations and 15/118 (13%) robustness issues
The 101 multimodal tasks span three domains (Video: 53, Doc & Image: 22, Code: 26), evaluated on 9 models.
No single model dominates: Video is led by ClaudeOpus-4.6/Sonnet-4.6 (15.4%), Doc & Image by GPT-5.4 (54.5%), Code by MiMo-V2-Omni (33.3%).
Aggregating across models (Figure 6), capability is unevenly distributed: Video Pass^3 averages only 10.7% vs. Doc & Image 32.3% and Code 23.9%.
Consistency also varies, measured by the conversion ratio ρ = Pass^3/Pass@3: Video 0.37, Code 0.48, Doc & Image 0.53

Of the 300 released tasks, 250 (83.3%) are entirely original designs authored from scratch, covering all three task groups.
The remaining 50 tasks (16.7%) are drawn from established benchmarks, with 10 from OfficeQA
and integrated into Claw-Eval with their original prompts and scoring criteria preserved.
